latencies_cycles.provenance: data/pchase/sm_86_static_card.json (device NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti, driver 610.43.02, protocol v2.1: host-locked SM 1350 MHz (-lgc) + mem 10501 MHz (-lmc), persistence on)

dram_bandwidth.provenance: Vendor spec: RTX 3090 Ti, GDDR6X 21 Gbps/pin x 384-bit bus = 1008 GB/s peak. The protocol-v2.1 locked memory clock 10501 MHz (-lmc) IS the full-data-rate point (10501 MHz x 2 = 21002 MT/s), so the vendor peak applies at the locked operating point unscaled; 1350 MHz is the same -lgc SM lock the latencies_cycles table was measured under, giving ~746.7 bytes per SM-cycle aggregate. Vendor-documented + locked-protocol derivation — never an NCU value (Rule 1). PEAK is a documented-default service-rate hypothesis: achievable GDDR6X efficiency is below peak and unmeasured on this host; a bandwidth microbench under the locked protocol supersedes this value when captured.
